instructions:
Pick the specified object and carry it to the robot's rest posture. You have only a target category, head/hand RGB-D, robot joint measurements and attempt-relative odometry. Identify the object and infer its location, dimensions and grasp orientation yourself. No demonstrations or earlier attempts are available; within this attempt all earlier observations and responses remain in context.
Return exactly one tool call per turn. Include note: 1-3 short sentences stating observed evidence and intended effect, not hidden chain-of-thought. done/give_up require hindsight and end immediately. All irrelevant parameters MUST be null, poses=[] unless a pose tool is used, and gripper MUST be null except for set_gripper.
Pose tools use CURRENT base_link: x forward, y left, z up, meters; position is gripper_link origin, quaternion [x,y,z,w] is unit length. Gripper local +x points through the fingers, fingers separate along local y. After base motion, recompute your pose goals in the current frame. Odometry is ideal noiseless displacement relative to attempt-start base_link, not a refreshed target location.
move_base(turn_rad,forward_m) turns then drives; negative distance reverses, no sideways motion. Limits: +/-pi rad, +/-1.5 m, speeds 1 rad/s and 0.5 m/s, arrival 0.03 rad and 0.02 m, 80 steps including settling. Upper-body targets and gripper are held. All actual motion starts with measured base settling, consuming the same budget; no scene collision filtering is performed.
look(pan_rad,tilt_rad) sets absolute head joint angles: pan [-1.57,1.57], tilt [-0.76,1.45] rad. It holds torso/arm targets and gripper; at most 40 steps including settling. If vision is obscured, choose another view; higher resolution cannot reveal hidden surfaces.
locate_point(camera,pixel,observation_id) uses head or hand, integer pixel [x,y] in the latest 640x640 image (origin top-left, 0..639). It reads that frame's raw depth, intrinsics and robot FK. The returned point is an observed SURFACE in current base_link, not an object center or automatic grasp pose. Invalid depth is not filled. After any movement query a fresh observation; old points cannot be assumed current. A 3x3 neighborhood depth spread is only sensor evidence, not an obstacle-free guarantee.
check_path(poses) checks robot IK, limits and continuity only. Both check_path and locate_point are read-only, use zero environment steps, and consume one tool slot. minimum_steps is a theoretical lower bound, NEVER a predicted execution time or guarantee. IK failure means no solution found, not proof of unreachability.
move_to uses one pose; move_eef_chunk uses 1..8 poses, 60 steps per call. set_gripper: 1=open, 0=closed, intermediate=partial; closing first aligns to the preceding motion target. return_to_rest retains the gripper and returns torso/head/arm toward official rest, at most 60 steps. Lifting or arrived alone is not strict success.
There are at most 25 tool calls and 200 official control steps; motion, settling and gripper steps all count. Invalid calls consume a tool slot but execute no action. Observe actual residuals and step breakdown before planning further. Reserve up to 60 steps for rest, including head return. An official stop ends action execution immediately.
GUIDANCE VERSION guidance-v4-compact. The following constants come only from the robot URDF, original robot collision shapes and robot camera configuration. The rigid chassis has conservative horizontal radius 0.288 m (diameter 0.576 m) about base_link and forward extent 0.287 m. This footprint does not bound the projecting arm. The shoulder pan origin in current base_link is approximately [0.03265, 0, 0.72601 + torso_lift] m, for torso_lift from 0 to 0.386 m: shoulder height 0.72601 to 1.11201 m. A triangle-inequality bound from the shoulder to gripper_link is 1.10994 m; from base_link's origin the horizontal upper bound is 1.14259 m. These are only length upper bounds, not proof of a feasible grasp; orientation, joint limits and height reduce useful reach. Check proposed poses with check_path.
At the official rest posture, the head camera position in base_link is [0.167310, 0.000000, 1.414161] m and it looks forward and down by 0.562 rad (forward unit direction [0.846191, 0, -0.532880]). Its vertical field of view is 2 rad; square 2048 by 2048 images have the same horizontal field of view. Camera clipping range is 0.01 to 100 m, but the displayed depth maps encode only 0 to 4 m, saturating beyond 4 m; 0 is invalid. This camera pose is for rest only, not a constant pose after head or torso motion.
Before moving the base, use the head depth image to estimate the nearest obstacle in the intended travel corridor, approximately one chassis diameter (0.576 m) wide. Camera-frame depth is not automatically forward clearance: consider the camera's height and downward angle, and the chassis front extent. Choose motion that leaves clearance for the chassis front; unknown depth is not evidence of free space. Objects are often on furniture; its near edge can be closer than the target center. Use the furniture edge as the stopping reference, then reach over it with the arm. Near obstacles, use |forward_m| <= 0.3 m per move_base call; observe the images, odometry and tool feedback after each segment before choosing the next. First use check_path on both pregrasp and grasp poses to test robot-only reach, before deciding to approach further. An accepted check_path does not check scene collisions. Reserve up to 60 of the official steps for return_to_rest; monitor remaining steps while aligning and grasping.

Each response also includes task_state: belief, uncertainty, expected_change, next_check, each at most 160 characters. These are brief evidence-linked self-reports, not hidden reasoning or measured truth. Cite observation IDs and camera names when relevant; say unknown when evidence is insufficient. First compare the previous expected change with the latest observation and measured result. Preserve unresolved uncertainty unless new evidence resolves it.
History rows identify control-step intervals; all earlier observation text, valid decisions and measured tool feedback are replayed as historical data, never pending commands. Only the previous and current image groups are included; older images are absent unless explicitly recalled. Current measurements override old estimates. Old pixels and base-frame points remain tied to their source observation; do not reuse them as current goals after motion without re-evaluation. No automatic scene-point update is provided.
Use both camera views where informative, but state when either cannot establish clearance. Target distance or a visible floor strip does not establish full-body clearance. Before a base move explain the relevant visual/depth evidence, remaining occlusion and why it supports the chosen distance.
A chunk executes continuously without intermediate Astra visual decisions. Use separate move_to calls when an intermediate pose needs visual confirmation; combine only when you judge that intermediate observation unnecessary. Balance additional calls and settling against the remaining budget. No force or stalled-progress event interrupts a command.

Each request is self-contained, with no hidden prior session. Historical image labels include their observation ID and turn; those images are not current sensor state. recall_observation(observation_id) requests one older image group from this attempt, costs a tool call but no environment step. All other parameters are null and poses=[]. Its images appear only on the next decision alongside previous/current views. It cannot replay motion, and locate_point still accepts only the latest observation. Your old notes and task_state are beliefs, not measured facts. Keep notes concise and use history to avoid repeating rejected plans.
